posts.title: Day 13 of Cop31 – recapped
posts.text: That’s all for today – we hope everyone following from Antalya gets a good night’s sleep. Here are the highlights from the 13th day of the 31st UN climate summit, which is still not over: Activists told the Presidency this summit could be one of the ‘most disappointing Cops’ ever Carbon removal must ‘be additional,…

“Today we have listened to you and sought to find common ground for your expectations,” said Murat Kurum, thanking the tired delegates for their “constructive approach”. He said the third and final version of the cover decision will be “in your hands shortly”, and parties will have until 6am local time to consider the…

Cop31 President, Murat Kurum, has arrived on the main stage, and has been immediately swarmed by delegates. The Turkish-Australian joint presidency has kept a low public profile today, on the first day of overtime, and the transparency they promised has been somewhat hard to come by for observers of the process.…
A handful of less controversial topics have indeed gone through without issue, and the session is taking a brief break before the Cop31 President arrives.

A dispute has broken about gender – and how it is defined – with interventions from Argentina and Paraguay. The draft document “encourages” a finance committee to enhance efforts to ensure gender-responsiveness in implementing its workplan, and requests Parties to consider gender balance and geographical…

Next up is a text on long-term climate finance, which has been rejected by the African Group. “This process did not provide sufficient space for negotiations,” said the negotiator for Ghana, speaking on the group’s behalf. “For now, it is not ready on our side for adoption.” The objection is to paragraph 3, which…

The plenary session has now actually begun, and we understood that it’s only the uncontroversial topics that are to be gaveled through. However, the very first topic, on climate empowerment – helping all members of society engage in climate action – has been met with an immediate objection from Russia that has drawn…

The Guardian has been leaked a submission that the countries calling themselves the “progressive coalition” – including the EU, UK and island and developing countries – want added to the cover text that is expected to be brought to a plenary at some point in the hours ahead. It is an eleventh-hour bid to bolster the…

The plenary has been pushed back by half an hour, into Sunday morning local time. Many diplomats have gone home, eager to get some rest before the (assumed) progress at the morning plenary session. Others are taking rest where they can find it.
The plenary session has just begun. A few weary-looking delegates have started to file in but the main stage has not yet been occupied …

Neither of these things are necessarily anything to brag about, but is Cop31 about to go down as both the biggest and the longest Cop in history? It is just after 11pm here in Antalya and we have been told that a plenary will commence at 11:30pm but that this will only deal with procedural issues. We are also getting…

Why does it matter if the Cop31 deal neglects to mention fossil fuels? Here’s a quick recap. The main purpose of these annual UN climate summits is to stop the planet from heating. When world leaders signed the Paris agreement at a Cop in 2015, they bound their countries to keeping global heating by the end of the…

Three of the world’s biggest carbon polluters agreed to boost oil production this week, during talks in China that appear to have been far more fruitful than the climate summit is shaping up to be. The fuel deal between the US, China and Russia was struck on Thursday in Shenzhen, China, just as diplomats attending…

A predicament “that never should have deteriorated so far” is how Jasper Inventor, head of the Greenpeace’s delegation, has described the current situation at Cop31, as weary delegates bemoan the lack of a new draft deal or clarity over the next steps. “The fact that no text has been distributed and no actual…
